body.x: Spotting early signs of fall risk or cognitive and motor decline in older adults depends on assessing the same person repeatedly over time, which is hard to arrange in everyday settings.
What if a wearable sensor could collect gait data during ordinary movement and a platform could turn it into a report and an exercise plan?

That is the approach of PHYSIO Inc., a Daejeon-based company founded in 2022 and led by CEO Jungkyoung Yoo. At KES 2026, PHYSIO is presenting PHYSIO LINK, a smart gait-analysis and body-correction device, together with PHYSIO CLASS, its digital healthcare platform.

An inertial measurement unit in PHYSIO LINK collects gait and movement data. PHYSIO CLASS analyzes gait speed, stride length, cadence, left-right balance, variability and knee movement and presents the results in a report that users can read without specialist training. The exhibit also covers running analysis, including knee movement, landing patterns and movement stability. The solution links risk screening to personalized exercise, repeated assessment and progress tracking. PHYSIO says it does not diagnose disease; it is designed to identify signals associated with falls and cognitive or motor decline and connect users to preventive care. The company is now developing a multimodal model that adds speech indicators such as speaking speed and clarity to gait data.

PHYSIO reported revenue of KRW 335 million (about USD 240,000) in 2025. As of August 2026, it had completed 183 paid sales of PHYSIO LINK and PHYSIO CLASS to domestic exercise centers and individual users, and it has operated more than 30 demonstration booths at domestic and international events. Its first export went to FIT IN MOTION, a clinic in the U.S. state of Georgia, and at CES 2025 it held consultations with 18 overseas buyers and secured one letter of intent and one export contract.

The company holds 10 registered patents, has eight applications pending and has filed one PCT international application. It has completed medical-device certification, ISO 13485 certification and K-Testbed verification, and its awards include the SK hynix I-Lab Grand Prize and selection at the 2026 Innovative Product Demo Day.

The United States is PHYSIO's priority market. The company plans to test product, pricing and content on Amazon U.S. with a local partner while selling through physical therapists and rehabilitation clinics, and then move into senior-care and community-based preventive-care programs. At home, it aims to connect projects with dementia support centers, public health centers, senior welfare centers and long-term-care facilities to paid operations. PHYSIO is seeking healthcare distributors with access to rehabilitation and senior-care networks. It lists country-specific medical-device and data-privacy requirements, finding reliable local partners and building after-sales support as its main challenges.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
